title: The Discoveries That Made Our World

series.title: The Body Revealed
series.note: How people worked out what is really inside us, from the first honest dissections to the discovery of germs.

episodes.title: Vesalius: The Doctor Who Looked for Himself
episodes.covers: For 1,300 years doctors trusted an ancient Roman's descriptions of the body. In the 1540s Andreas Vesalius cut open real bodies in Padua, found Galen was wrong in hundreds of places, and published the first accurate book of human anatomy.
episodes.source: Vesalius, De humani corporis fabrica (1543), and histories of Renaissance anatomy

script.title: Vesalius: The Doctor Who Looked for Himself
script.description: For 1,300 years, doctors learned the human body from an ancient Roman's books, without checking. In the 1540s a young professor in Padua climbed down from his chair, picked up the knife, and found the books were wrong.

episodes.title: William Harvey and the Circle of Blood
episodes.covers: Everyone believed the liver made new blood all the time. William Harvey measured how much the heart pumped, did the sums, and showed in 1628 that the same blood goes round and round.
episodes.source: Harvey, De Motu Cordis (1628), and histories of physiology

script.title: William Harvey and the Circle of Blood
script.description: For fourteen hundred years, doctors believed the liver made fresh blood all day long. An English doctor did some simple sums about the heart, and showed the same blood goes round and round.

episodes.title: Leeuwenhoek's Tiny Animals
episodes.covers: A Dutch cloth merchant ground his own lenses, looked at a drop of pond water in the 1670s, and saw a world of living things nobody had imagined.
episodes.source: Leeuwenhoek's letters to the Royal Society and histories of microscopy

script.title: Leeuwenhoek's Tiny Animals
script.description: A Dutch cloth seller with no scientific training made his own tiny lenses, looked into a drop of lake water in 1674, and saw it swarming with life nobody had ever seen.

episodes.title: Semmelweis: The Doctor Who Said Wash Your Hands
episodes.covers: In 1840s Vienna, women were dying of fever after giving birth on one ward and not the other. Ignaz Semmelweis worked out why, told doctors to wash their hands, and was mocked for it.
episodes.source: Semmelweis's 1861 book on childbed fever and medical histories

script.title: Semmelweis: The Doctor Who Said Wash Hands
script.description: In 1840s Vienna, mothers were dying of fever after giving birth on one hospital ward, and far fewer on the ward next door. One young doctor worked out why, and almost nobody listened.

episodes.title: John Snow and the Broad Street Pump
episodes.covers: In 1854 cholera killed hundreds in Soho, London. A doctor mapped every death, found they clustered round one water pump, and had its handle removed.
episodes.source: John Snow, On the Mode of Communication of Cholera (1855)

episodes.title: Pasteur and the Invisible Enemy
episodes.covers: Louis Pasteur showed that tiny living things turn wine sour and make us ill, saved France's silk and wine industries, and made the first rabies vaccine.
episodes.source: Histories of Louis Pasteur and germ theory

series.title: The Universe Revealed
series.note: How we found our place in space, one stubborn observer at a time.

episodes.title: Copernicus Moves the Earth
episodes.covers: A Polish churchman spent decades on a book that put the Sun, not the Earth, at the centre, and only saw it printed as he was dying in 1543.
episodes.source: Copernicus, De revolutionibus (1543), and histories of astronomy

script.title: Copernicus Moves the Earth
script.description: For more than a thousand years, everyone knew the Earth stood still at the centre of everything. A Polish churchman worked out that it didn't, then waited thirty years to say so, and saw his book only as he was dying.

episodes.title: Galileo and the Telescope
episodes.covers: In 1609 Galileo pointed a homemade telescope at the sky, saw moons circling Jupiter and mountains on the Moon, and ended up on trial.
episodes.source: Galileo, Sidereus Nuncius (1610), and the records of his 1633 trial

episodes.title: Kepler and the Shape of the Orbits
episodes.covers: Johannes Kepler spent years trying to make Mars move in a perfect circle, and finally accepted that planets travel in ellipses.
episodes.source: Kepler, Astronomia Nova (1609), and histories of Tycho Brahe's data

episodes.title: Newton and the Pull of Everything
episodes.covers: Isaac Newton worked out that the force pulling an apple down is the same force holding the Moon in its orbit, and wrote the laws that explain both.
episodes.source: Newton, Principia (1687), and histories of the plague years at Woolsthorpe

episodes.title: Henrietta Leavitt Measures the Stars
episodes.covers: Paid to count stars on glass plates at Harvard, Henrietta Leavitt noticed a pattern in flickering stars that let astronomers measure the distance to anything.
episodes.source: Leavitt's 1912 paper and histories of the Harvard computers

episodes.title: Hubble and the Expanding Universe
episodes.covers: In the 1920s Edwin Hubble showed that our galaxy is one of countless others, and that they are all rushing away from each other.
episodes.source: Hubble's 1929 paper and histories of cosmology

series.title: Taming Electricity
series.note: From sparks in a laboratory to a wired world.

episodes.title: Benjamin Franklin and the Kite
episodes.covers: Franklin wanted to prove lightning was electricity, flew a kite into a storm in 1752, and invented the lightning rod.
episodes.source: Franklin's letters on electricity and histories of early electrical science

episodes.title: Volta Builds the First Battery
episodes.covers: A quarrel over twitching frogs' legs led Alessandro Volta to stack metal discs and soaked card in 1800, and make the first steady electric current.
episodes.source: Volta's 1800 letter to the Royal Society and histories of Galvani and Volta

episodes.title: Michael Faraday and the Spinning Wire
episodes.covers: A bookbinder's apprentice with no formal schooling made a wire spin round a magnet, and discovered how to make electricity from movement.
episodes.source: Faraday's diary and Experimental Researches in Electricity

episodes.title: The War of the Currents
episodes.covers: Thomas Edison backed direct current, Nikola Tesla and George Westinghouse backed alternating current, and the fight to light America turned ugly.
episodes.source: Histories of Edison, Tesla, Westinghouse and the 1893 Chicago World's Fair

episodes.title: Marconi Sends a Signal Across the Ocean
episodes.covers: A young Italian believed radio waves could carry messages around the curve of the Earth, and in 1901 heard three clicks across the Atlantic.
episodes.source: Histories of Guglielmo Marconi and early wireless

episodes.title: The Transistor: A Switch That Changed Everything
episodes.covers: At Bell Labs in 1947, three physicists made a tiny switch from a crystal, and it became the building block of every computer and phone.
episodes.source: Histories of Bell Labs and the 1947 point-contact transistor

series.title: Inside the Atom
series.note: How scientists cracked open the smallest thing in nature, and what came out.

episodes.title: Marie Curie and the Glowing Element
episodes.covers: Working in a leaky shed in Paris, Marie and Pierre Curie boiled tonnes of ore to find radium and polonium, and Marie became the first person to win two Nobel prizes.
episodes.source: Marie Curie's writings and biographies, and Nobel Prize records

episodes.title: Rutherford Finds the Nucleus
episodes.covers: In 1909 Ernest Rutherford's team fired tiny particles at gold foil, and a few bounced straight back. It was like a shell bouncing off tissue paper.
episodes.source: Rutherford's 1911 paper and histories of the Geiger-Marsden experiment

episodes.title: Lise Meitner Splits the Atom
episodes.covers: In 1938, a refugee from Nazi Germany walked in the snow with her nephew and worked out that the uranium atom had split in two, and was left out of the Nobel prize.
episodes.source: Meitner and Frisch's 1939 paper and histories of nuclear fission

episodes.title: The Neutron and the Chain Reaction
episodes.covers: James Chadwick found the neutron in 1932, and a physicist waiting at a London traffic light realised neutrons could set off a chain reaction.
episodes.source: Histories of Chadwick and Leo Szilard

episodes.title: The Night the Desert Turned to Glass
episodes.covers: In July 1945 scientists in New Mexico tested the first atomic bomb, and its flash turned the desert sand to green glass.
episodes.source: Histories of the Manhattan Project and the Trinity test

episodes.title: The Atom That Lights Your Home
episodes.covers: How the same physics became nuclear power stations, from the first reactor under a Chicago stadium to the power grid.
episodes.source: Histories of Chicago Pile-1 and civil nuclear power

series.title: Reading the Earth
series.note: How people learned to read the planet's own history in its rocks, fossils and ice.

episodes.title: Mary Anning: The Fossil Hunter of Lyme
episodes.covers: A carpenter's daughter on the Dorset coast found the first complete ichthyosaur skeleton as a girl, and helped prove creatures could become extinct.
episodes.source: Histories of Mary Anning and early palaeontology

episodes.title: Darwin and the Finches
episodes.covers: A young naturalist's five-year voyage on HMS Beagle gave him the clues, and it took him twenty more years to publish what they meant.
episodes.source: Darwin, The Voyage of the Beagle and On the Origin of Species (1859)

episodes.title: Wegener and the Drifting Continents
episodes.covers: In 1912 a weather scientist noticed the coasts of Africa and South America fit like a jigsaw, said the continents moved, and was laughed at for decades.
episodes.source: Wegener, The Origin of Continents and Oceans, and histories of plate tectonics

episodes.title: Marie Tharp Maps the Ocean Floor
episodes.covers: Kept off research ships because she was a woman, Marie Tharp drew the first map of the Atlantic floor from sounding data and found a great rift running down it.
episodes.source: Histories of Marie Tharp and Bruce Heezen's ocean floor maps

episodes.title: The Asteroid That Ended the Dinosaurs
episodes.covers: In 1980 a father and son found a thin layer of a rare metal in rock all over the world, and argued that a giant asteroid had wiped out the dinosaurs.
episodes.source: Alvarez et al. (1980) and the discovery of the Chicxulub crater

episodes.title: What Ice Remembers
episodes.covers: Scientists drilled kilometres down into Antarctic and Greenland ice and found bubbles of ancient air that record the planet's climate for 800,000 years.
episodes.source: Histories of polar ice core research and the EPICA and Vostok cores
